newsitem.title: Australia: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 5.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer met last week with the Australian ambassadors to a dozen Asian countries, and it was revealed all of them believe the rise of Independent MP Pauline Hanson put trade relations in the countries where they live, worth around A$56 billion a year, at risk. Page 1.

While Federal Treasurer Peter Costello and Prime Minister John Howard yesterday continued their push to ensure that a goods and services tax remains the centrepiece of tax reform discussions, Costello also strengthened his stance against holding a tax reform summit. Page 3.

In a move that break ranks with Prime Minister John Howard's call for government unity on the media ownership debate, Coalition backbencher Brendan Nelson has attacked the reform process in his weekly column in the North Shore Times. In the column, Nelson criticised Communications Minister Richard Alston's plan which would enable Kerry Packer to take over the John Fairfax newspaper group. Page 3.

Defence Minister Ian McLachlan has outlined plans to increase defence spending to pay for expensive high-technology equipment needed to maintain the regional technological superiority of the Australian Defence Force. McLachlan estimates Australian firms would win 60-70 per cent of the business that would flow from the new equipment. Page 2.

In a move strengthening his campaign for tax reform, Prime Minister John Howard yesterday linked the need to reform the existing tax system with the need to boost employment growth, following the release of figures economic activity has slowed to its weakest pace in over four years. Page 1.

The Productivity Commission has found Optus and Telstra are charging consumers collectively close to A$375 million more than they need to charge for international calls each year. The Commission's report, International Telecommunications Reform in Austraia, says the introduction of full competition on July 1 could see the cost of international calls halved. Page 1.

A series of meetings between Prime Minister John Howard, Federal Treasurer Peter Costello and Industry Minister John Moore has seen the Howard Government decide to cut car tariffs from 15 per cent in 2000 to 10 per cent in 2005. The decision comes after bitter struggle between the Government's top economic ministers over calls for an effective tariff freeze. Page 1.

After 10 years of secret research, Australian scientists have developed a machine one-millionth of a millimetre in size, which promises to revolutionise the diagnosis of diseases. Once it is commercially available, the machine could allow doctors to conduct their own tests for virtually all diseases in just a few minutes. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has been pushed to promote a lower Australian dollar to revive the manufacturing sector and ensure the retention of blue collar jobs following the release of figures showing the industry is now officially in recession. Pag 1.

Bruce Burrell, the man whose property was searched by police investigating the kidnapping of Sydney woman Kerry Whelan, yesterday faced charges involving two stolen vehicles, a rifle and a crossbow. The rifle is one allegedly taken from Mrs Whelan's millonaire husband, Bernard Whelan. Page 1.

The Judicial Commission of New South Wales is investigating a magistrate who ordered the arrest, fingerprinting, photographing and detention of two women in police cells who were allegedly victims of a domestic assault, but failed to appear as witnesses i the case against the man. Page 1.

Following Federal Government plans to allow increases in foreign ownership of television stations in Australia, Seven Network owner Kerry Stokes has vowed to pull out of his ownership of the network, saying if the new plans are installed he would have to eview his position. Page 1.
THE AGE

Following the release yesterday by the Victorian Government of details of Intergraph's state-wide A$170 million contract, it was revealed Melbourne's ambulance service and fire brigade are withholding payments to the computer-aided dispatch operator because of a failure to meet key emergency performance benchmarks. Page 1.

The Productivity Commission has found telecommunications companies Telstra and Optus have been making huge profits on international phone calls by charging consumers an average of five times the cost of providing the service. The Commission found that the companies have failed to pass on the savings achieved by improved technology. Page 1.

In what is an international first, a joint-venture between the CSIRO, Sydney University, and a subsidiary of Melbourne-based company Pacific Dunlop has created a biosensor, the world's smallest machine, which is destined to revolutionise manufacturing andtechnology. Page 1.

While the Ashes cricket tour against England does not have the significance for the Australian team of previous tours such as those to the West Indies and South Africa, the team is still facing the series with nervous anticipation. Page 1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
